title: 1988 AHSME Problem 22
statement: For how many integers \(x\) does a triangle with side lengths \(10,\) \(24,\) and \(x\) have all its angles acute?

solutions.text:
Acuteness requires \(x^2<10^2+24^2=676\) and \(24^2<10^2+x^2,\) so \(x<26\) and \(x^2>476.\) For integer \(x,\) this gives \(22\le x\le25.\) All four values also satisfy the triangle inequality, so there are \(4\) values.

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: Apply the strict Pythagorean inequality to the largest side in each possible ordering
The angle opposite \(24\) and the angle opposite \(x\) give the restrictive bounds
